utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: No one else.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one else.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Nobody else --

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And it wasn't drawn in an office. It was drawn in Milan Lecic's apartment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: No one else - is this right - contributed to the idea of drawing this plan apart from you, whose idea it was, and Milan Lecic, who did the drawing?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Two details first of all. If you look at the big blue shape, this one you pointed to first, this one here, does that in any way come to be described as a horseshoe in either police or military terminology?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I see here would be an ellipse rather than a horseshoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Does the word "horseshoe" have a significance for you in relation to Racak?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: What we can see -- I'm sorry, I think that you got a bit confused. This big blue circle was not drawn very precisely. It just shows where Racak is. The smaller circle is Luzak, and this other ellipsis is where Petrovo is. And Hadzovici mahala. The deployment of forces was depicted quite differently and marked differently, the deployment of forces in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: It is a small point for the time being, although it may become interesting later. If we look at the -- with the map orientated north-south and if we look at the left-hand side of that big blue shape that's more like an ellipse you say - that's fine, I'm not troubled about that - it is undoubtedly all to the east of Rance, isn't it? There is no way in which that line, that westerly line of the blue ellipse passes between Rance and Luznica? Luznica is way off to the left, isn't it? Your Honours can see this on page 11 of the usual map at about 21 -- Rance is on R-20 and -- sorry, on Q-20 and Luznica is on P-20.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Luznica, Mr. Nice, has nothing to do with this case or the Racak case. Nothing whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you for making it clear.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because Luznica is far away from Racak. Let's not exaggerate, but about 15 kilometres. To the north at that, north of Racak. North of Racak.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And would it be -- would I be right in saying that nothing of a military character happened as far west as that?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not informed of any operation that took place there. This is not the area of my secretariat. That is the SUP of Prizren. I think it's Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You weren't aware of anything happening that far away, a blockade or anything of that sort?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Luznica?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I mean, the only reason I ask you, and I intended to put this off until later but I see I won't reach it otherwise until the end of -- until tomorrow, but you see, if you were to take your own D -- 1A is a tab we've looked at, you see. Let me just check what the right one is. Well, we can look at tab 5 in your own documents. That's an easier way of dealing with it. You've seen the document before, but tab 5 will do very nicely for the time being. And this is a document, I think, that if we just look towards the end of it, is signed by Bozidar Trajkovic. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And -- Your Honours, I'm sorry. The reference is incorrect in the index, and I will have to come back to that next week because I can't immediately -- I thought it was at tab 5, but -- I beg Your Honour's pardon? Not by next week, tomorrow. Tomorrow. Just give me a moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell me what you're interested in. Perhaps I could help you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'll show it to you and then we'll deal with it. This is a document. Would you have a look at this. It will come your way and go on the overhead projector.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honours, it was tab 5 in the Racak documents that were produced on an earlier occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: This is a document, you see -- if you have a look at it, you'll see it's a document that comes from your SUP, and it's dated the 15th of January, apparently, so it's hot off the press for Racak. It appears to be signed by yourself. Is it your signature there? Or typed signature?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And then if you go down to -- if you go to the -- it's also Exhibit 156, tab 16, or Exhibit 320, tab 27. I'm grateful to Ms. Dicklich for that. If you go on the original version to, I think, the bottom of the first page or the second page, probably -- second page, I think for you, you'll see a paragraph that begins - in the English, it's towards the bottom of the first page - "The horseshoe ambush was applied in the blockade and it was laid between the villages of Luznica and Rance ..." Now, that's what you wrote. You can see that, I think. Can you find that bit of text?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the text, but it is probably a typing error or a printing error. Luznica is not in the SUP of Urosevac. There's no point in mentioning it. It must be a typing error.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, you've got it there in the Serb original, haven't you, and it does say, does it, "The horseshoe ambush was applied in the blockade and it was laid between the villages of Luznica and Rance, behind terrorist trenches"?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And you signed off on that, didn't you? Bit of a mistake, was it?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not Luznica Mr. Nice. Well, I mean, it does say here that it's Luznica, but I'm telling you that it's a typing error. This is Luzak and the village of Petrovo, Petrovo Selo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Racak is not totally encircled. The terrorists were allowed one escape route, as is usually the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: That's why you used the word "horseshoe," yes? Give them a way out. Because you did use the word "horseshoe." You could have one mistake in a sentence, but two?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please. If trenches had been dug in the shape of a horseshoe, if the trenches look like a horseshoe, and if the police goes into these trenches rather than the terrorists, is that a mistake? Can it still be called a horseshoe? Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A horseshoe. The trenches were horseshoe shaped. You can see that on your own pictures. Yesterday I had a look at this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Mr. Janicevic, let me make something clear to you that should be clear to you as an experienced policeman. In my cross-examination, I'm going to be seeking explanation from documents that are contemporaneous, and as a policeman in charge of investigating crime, you must know that what people say at the time is always very valuable. Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's just clarify another thing, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have a topographic map --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm going to pursue you on this because you are an experienced policeman. Do you accept that what people say and what you said at the time is important? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Now, I want to know, and it's a small point, what you meant on the 15th of January when, in dealing with what had been happening generally in the area of Racak, you referred to a horseshoe ambush applied in the blockade, and it was laid behind the villages of -- forget Luznica if you say that's a mistake. I don't accept it, but if you say it -- behind the villages of something and Rance, behind terrorist trenches and connecting trenches. You're describing a horseshoe ambush by your forces.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, earlier on I asked you a question about the horseshoe and you wouldn't accept that horseshoe was appropriate. Would you now please explain to me what you meant when you actually wrote on the day about a horseshoe?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I meant the Operative Pursuit Group that took the terrorist trenches that had been dug and placed in the form of a horseshoe. They were dug in such a way that from these positions practically the entire road could be fired at, and part of Stimlje too. That's really in the form of a horseshoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm going to move on, because otherwise we'll be forever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I would like to know, before you do, where the horseshoe was located. Where is it you said the ambush was actually set up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the terrorist trenches above Racak. In this area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry, could you show me that again? Now, what -- what, then, are the two villages that you meant to refer to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Racak, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The document says clearly, "The horseshoe ambush was applied in the blockade and it was laid between the villages of Luznica and Rance ..." and you say that that's a mistake. So which villages did you mean to refer to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Between Luzak and Racak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And where is Luzak? Oh, yes, I see it now. Yes. How could such a mistake be made in preparing your report? You've prided yourself on your supreme efficiency throughout your evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The mistake was only made in terms of time, in terms of the dynamics involved. All the rest is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But it was --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The person made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: This report was written by you on the day, on the 15th of January, 1999.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean the mistake in this report? Well, Your Honour, typing errors do occur. The man who typed this typed this on a teleprinter, so it was directly taken off a teleprinter. There's probably some other mistake there as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can we go back to maps --

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. I haven't got the original part of the official report or the Official Note. The report that I dictated, and it was -- was retyped by the man at the teleprinter and he sent the telegram, the dispatch. So it's in the teleprinter that the mistake was made, that's for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And your original one, what, did it go up in smoke?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether it disappeared. Maybe it can be sent to you as well, like many other documents were, thousands. I didn't really look.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, we'll look at those documents in more detail. There's another point I want to make before we close today and I'd like you to go back, please, to the map, Mr. Lecic's flat, at the table, the map is laid out with these coloured inks and these colours pens. I'd like you to tell us, please, this: If we look at -- have you got the first map, the 0300 to 0830 map there in front of you?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And we see various references there to times, and just remind us, if we look towards the bottom of the ellipse shape, we see a blue circle with a red cross, and to the left of the blue circle we see a horizontal line, 0645 underneath and 2 above. What does 2 mean?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a terrorist bunker, a terrorist observation point where two members of that terrorist brigade got killed. That's where the 2 is. And where the number 1 is was where 1 member got killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And then to the right of that, where there's a 4, that's where 4 people got killed. And then up to the north-east where there's a -- is a -- over 715 or 716, is that a 1 or what is it there? There's another 1 there. How many people got killed there?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 1, yes. One.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Whose idea was it to put this in?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The idea to put these numbers in?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mine and Lecic's too.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Lecic's. That's interesting.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the dynamic of --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Has Lecic been following the trial, do you know?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did you have any input from the legal associates of the accused as to what should go on this map or was it entirely your own idea?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not get any instructions from the legal associates as to what the map should contain. The instructions I received were that the truth should be said about Racak. I have taken an oath, and I'm telling the truth. It suits someone, it doesn't suit others.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you for the comment but let's get on with the evidence. Let's look at that one person who died there. That's not something you could remember, is it?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well -- sorry. Probably? Probably you could remember?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably I didn't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Probably you didn't remember. Likewise the 4, probably you didn't remember. Likewise the 1, probably you didn't remember. You didn't remember any of these locations of deaths because you weren't there, were you? Were you?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not there, but on the basis of the reports that I received --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, let's come to that in a minute because we'll deal with it in stages. There are two more maps, one of which has deaths shown on it. May we take it, but don't say yes if you're going to subsequently say no, may we take it that you could not place the position of or number of deaths on any of these maps yourself, could you, three weeks ago?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you. You didn't have any document in your possession that could place or give the number of deaths in the course of the ambush, did you?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had a document, but I could not establish the exact localities because I was not there on the spot myself. That's why I called a man who was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reports. I had the reports. After every anti-terrorist operation, those who were in charge of the operation would submit reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Which report, tell me, would show where people died and in what numbers? Which report?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The on-site investigation of the investigating judge. The report of the company commander --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and the platoon commanders after the action.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: What about the company and the platoon --

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Marinkovic's report --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, I missed the first part of your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Danica Marinkovic's report has not gone up in smoke. It exists. That's the investigative judge. Now, let's turn to the company and platoon commanders' reports. Where are they?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reports of the platoon commanders and the company commander, as I said, were submitted to the working group attached to the MUP staff in Pristina. All the reports on the basis of which that commission made its own assessment had to do with the anti-terrorist operation in Racak. They were assessing the anti-terrorist operation in Racak and its success.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Please help me. Are you saying that the platoon commander's reports and the company commander's reports showed in detail the position of these people who died, or are you saying they may have shown the positions, or don't you know? Which is it?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only the places are described in terms of how many terrorists got killed in the fighting and where.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: So there's no map in these earlier reports, whether they've gone up in smoke or whether they're still sitting in the prosecutor's office, or whether a copy of them is in your own archives, there is no map showing the position of the dead, is there?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: So when you came with Lecic --

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no contemporaneous map from that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, is there a later map apart from these nice, new, three-week old maps? Is there any other map that's going to show where people died, please?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, I said that this was made three weeks ago. I said that at the very outset. I said that it was done in preparation of the trial. I never said that they were old maps. I said that it was done on the basis of the recollection of the people who were --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- in charge of that, part of the people who were in charge.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Is there any other earlier map, showing where people died?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Perhaps you have one.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: From your evidence, then, it sounds, doesn't it, as though -- I think His Honour may have a question, but it sounds as though, for the position of the bodies on this map, we are dependent on your bringing Lecic's recollection. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're not right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, if I've missed something, apart from the fact that you're bringing Lecic's recollection drawn on this map to show where people died and in what numbers, perhaps you'd explain it for me.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This map and all three maps were made on the basis of the recollection of the members of the police who took part in the anti-terrorist operation. There is no other documentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Wait a minute.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no other documentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Very well. The police, are you saying that these maps have as an input into them more than the memory of Lecic? Was his flat populated by the two of you and some other officers sitting there, adding their comments, or was it just Lecic? Please help me.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, please. There is no way I can help you. I told you the truth about this map. The man whose name I gave you drew the map on his own. I don't know how to draw maps. There was no one in his apartment except for him. It is certain that over the past six or seven years he talked to other policemen who were involved in the operation. He's the only one who is competent and who knows what happened there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You just mentioned, Mr. Janicevic, the memory of the police, the recollection of the members of the police who took part in the anti-terrorist operation. Did you also receive information from them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I didn't receive anything from them. I received all my information from the company commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, unless I didn't understand, it says here as one of your answers: "This map and all three maps were made on the basis of the recollection of the members of the police who took part in the anti-terrorist operation. There is no other documentation."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. On the basis of the recollection of Milan Lecic, commander of the company, and the policemen who took part. He had time to talk to them and he probably did talk to them. He probably saw someone or spoke to someone, but when the map was being drawn, only he and I were present, no one else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It was Lecic who sent you reports by radio?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You -- you said that when you were preparing -- or when the map was being prepared, you had the investigating judge's report and the reports of the platoon commander and company commander.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was the chronology of events made contemporaneously based on reports of company commanders and platoon commanders' reports.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But you had these documents in front of you at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At what time? You mean at the time when we were doing this or in 1999?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: At the time when you were --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In 1999 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No. At the time you were preparing the maps three weeks ago, did you have the platoon commander's report and the company commander's report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had the chronology of events.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And where did you get that from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had it in my case file. My file. It's the document that I wrote myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is it here? Is it one of the -- that's one of the tabs we have here. Now, what did you mean by the platoon commander's report and the company commander's report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I mentioned the reports of platoon commanders and company commanders. At the time when the chronology of events document was being drawn up, that's the document we have under one of the tabs here, it was made on the basis of platoon commanders' and company commanders' reports in 1999, on the 19th of January.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, we'll have to stop. We will adjourn and resume tomorrow morning at 9.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 4th day of October, 2005, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.48 p.m.,
